rules.statement: When sources disagree: deposit, then PI correspondence, then Methods, then precedent.
A value is copied verbatim from its source, in the source's own field names and spelling.
Read Methods, Data Availability, captions, the SI and the deposits before building the tree.
Never assume: no evidence, no value. A cell with no source is blank, with its reason.
A blank is never a placeholder: no TBD, unknown, N/A or *** in a published paper's cells.
Never ask the PI about a published paper; report a gap instead.
Cells from an animal go MUS to TIS to CEL, never MUS straight to CEL.
Antibodies, chemicals and antibody panels (AB, CHM, ABP) are attributes, never samples.
An instrument technique is the assay on an edge, not a sample tier of its own.
An analysis-tier sample exists only where the deposits hold an analysis file for it.
Reuse an existing record, with evidence of the match, before minting a new one.
DOI and PMID go only on rows this paper produced, and only the paper's own.
One study per paper, titled with the paper's title.
Never add attributes to shared sample types: use only the attributes the type has.
Choose sample types by technology; follow a precedent study only on the same platform.
A protocol is Methods paragraphs copied verbatim; no Methods text, no protocol.
A UID stamp is its deposit's date; upstream rows take the earliest; no deposit, the publication date.
CSBC registers a data sample only when its raw file is deposited.
MetNet registers metadata-only rows that point to the paper's DOI.
